ROOT-CAUSE PASS ON ALEX'S ITEM 3, 2026-08-30, run under the root-cause skill at Anthony's request. TWO SYMPTOMS WERE REPORTED AS ONE FAILURE. They have different causes, and the reporter's own inference about the second is probably wrong.

═══ ① THE SYMPTOM, WITH HIS DIAGNOSIS CUT OUT ═══
In one parallel tool batch containing `add_change_event id=chg:X` and `pin_at_epoch node=chg:X`, the pin returned `Node not found: ChangeEvent chg:X` in `content`. A later retry found it present. A subsequent `set_artifact_checksum` naming that id returned the STRUCTURED-CONTENT STUB — not a refusal — and the next `export_graph` still carried the OLD checksum. His text says *"the pin raced the create"*; that is a hypothesis, and it is removed here so it had to survive a measurement.

═══ ② PRECEDENT, AND IT REFUTES THE LEADING CANDIDATE ═══
`fact:the-decision-race-is-caller-ordering-not-read-after-write` (2026-08-09, twenty-one days earlier, SAME USER'S FLEET) already established the mechanism for the identical class:

  · READ-AFTER-WRITE ALREADY HOLDS. A capture tool takes an exclusive `write_lock()`, writes, and the guard drops BEFORE the response returns. There is no visibility window to close.
  · THE RWLOCK SERIALISES ACCESS, NOT INTENT. Parallel batches carry no ordering, so the modify can legitimately win the lock first — at which instant the node genuinely does not exist and `Node not found` is the CORRECT answer, not a bug.

So the first symptom is fully explained and is not a defect in the write path.

═══ ③ THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT ON THE SECOND SYMPTOM ═══
His conclusion: *"first checksum call almost certainly failed (ChangeEvent missing, or export raced), and the failure was invisible."*

Measured in code 2026-08-30:
  · crates/reflow2-core/src/artifact.rs, DesignUpdated branch: the ChangeEvent existence IS checked and a missing one returns `DynoError::NodeNotFound`.
  · The MCP layer validates only that the field is PRESENT; the existence check is in core.
  · `NodeNotFound` reaches `content` — proven by his own report, where `pin_at_epoch`'s identical error WAS visible to him.

⭐ THEREFORE THE CHECKSUM CALL DID NOT FAIL ON A MISSING CHANGEEVENT. Had it done so he would have seen that refusal in the same channel and the same shape as the pin. He saw a stub, which is the SUCCESS rendering. THE WRITE ALMOST CERTAINLY LANDED, AND THE `export_graph` THAT SHOWED THE OLD HASH RAN BEFORE IT. He named this possibility himself and then set it aside.

═══ ④ WHY THAT MATTERS — IT MOVES THE DANGER ═══
If the write never failed, then "serialise dependent writes" fixes the pin and DOES NOT fix the thing that actually threatens a committed export. The dangerous shape is not write-then-write; it is WRITE-THEN-EXPORT. `export_graph` acquires the same lock and is ordered by nothing, so an export issued in the same turn as writes can serialise a graph state missing those writes — and that document is the one that gets COMMITTED. A wrong committed export is worse than a failed pin, and it produces exactly the state the drift gate exists to catch.

═══ ⑤ THE CLASS, AND WHY IT RECURRED ═══
The 2026-08-09 note named the general fix in as many words: *"THE GENERAL FIX IS A DESCRIPTION, NOT A FEATURE: no tool description says that parallel batches carry no ordering, or that a create-then-modify pair must be sequenced."*

What was built instead was the INSTANCE fix — `cap:a-decision-can-be-created-already-settled`, collapsing `add_decision` + `set_decision_status` into one unmisorderable call. That pair is now safe. Twenty-one days later the same user hit the same class through a DIFFERENT pair (`add_change_event` + `pin_at_epoch`) and a different shape entirely (writes + `export_graph`).

🛑 SO THE CAUSE OF THE RECURRENCE IS THAT THE FIX ADDRESSED THE PAIR AND THE DESCRIPTION WAS NEVER WRITTEN. Test ⑥ of the root-cause skill applied: would the 08-09 fix have prevented the 08-30 report? No. It stops one pair out of an open set.

═══ ⑥ WHY IT IS INVISIBLE TO THIS USER SPECIFICALLY ═══
Ordering hazards are survivable when you can read the result. On a client that forwards only `content` (his item 1, now on its third report) a successful write and a no-op are indistinguishable, so the ONE recovery available — read it back — is closed. The two defects are independent and only dangerous together, which is why this arrived as one confusing report rather than two clear ones.

═══ ⑦ NOT ESTABLISHED ═══
· STILL NOT REPRODUCED WITH A CONCURRENT CLIENT. The 08-09 note flagged exactly this limit and it still stands: both passes read the mechanism from code rather than driving two overlapping calls at one server. The reproduction is two overlapping tool calls asserting the failure disappears when sequenced, and nobody has run it.
· Whether the checksum write landed is INFERRED from the refusal channel behaving as his own report shows, not observed in his graph.
· Whether `export_graph` can in fact be ordered before a write in the same batch is reasoned from the shared lock, not measured.
